name: Mantis Shallows
description: Mantis Shallows is a warm oceanic world where the global sea averages only eighty meters in depth, its floor a visible mosaic of coral plateaus and sand channels even from low orbit. Thousands of atoll rings break the surface, their rims crowned with dense tangles of amphibious vegetation that roots in the shallows and reaches into the humid air. The water is so clear that sunlight penetrates to the seabed everywhere, fueling photosynthetic mats that carpet the ocean floor in shifting greens and golds.

The air is thick with moisture and the sweet, almost cloying fragrance of aquatic blossoms that open at the surface in floating meadows. At night the entire ocean ignites with bioluminescence, turning the world into a luminous mirror that reflects the stars back at themselves. The sound of water lapping against atoll walls is constant and meditative, punctuated by the clicking of crustacean-analogues and the soft exhale of tidal breathing through hollow coral structures.

A pharmaceutical research outpost operates on the largest atoll chain, studying the extraordinary medicinal properties of the native flora. Several compounds have already yielded breakthrough treatments for degenerative neural conditions, and the researchers believe they have catalogued less than one percent of the available biochemistry. The shallowness of the ocean and the absence of predatory megafauna make Mantis Shallows unusually safe for an alien world, a fact that has not gone unnoticed by development interests.

Competing pharmaceutical firms are lobbying to establish harvesting operations, which the current research team argues would devastate the delicate shallow-water ecosystems before they can be fully studied. The atoll chains also sit atop geothermal vents that could provide energy for industrial-scale operations, making the economic case for development increasingly difficult to resist. Mantis Shallows is a paradise on a timer, and the clock is ticking.
